create.description: Turn rows, text or data into a file you can attach to an email, upload to a drive, or download: a CSV or Excel spreadsheet, a text file, or JSON.
create.name: create

parameters.description: CSV and Excel files are spreadsheets made from rows. A text file holds text. JSON holds data for another system to read.
parameters.name: format

parameters.description: The rows to write, such as the rows a sheet or an earlier step returned. Each row's fields become the columns, and their names the header row.
parameters.name: rows

parameters.description: The data to save, such as an earlier step's result.
parameters.name: data

parameters.description: What to call the file, such as Weekly leads. The right extension is added for you. Leave empty to call it data (or file, for text).
parameters.name: filename

returns.description: The new file, kept for 30 days. Give document_ref to a step that takes a file, such as an email's attachments or a drive upload.

content_type.description: The file's media type, such as text/csv.

document_ref.description: The file, for a later step that takes one.

documents.description: The same file as a one-item list, the shape steps that download files return.

read.description: Get what's inside a file: the rows of a CSV or Excel sheet, the text of a PDF or Word document, or the data in a JSON file. Works with an upload, an email attachment, or a file an earlier step downloaded.

mock_response.text:
Name,Email,Company
Jordan Lee,jordan@acme.test,Acme Corp
Sam Rivera,sam@northwind.test,Northwind

read.name: read

parameters.description: The file to read. Upload one, or pick a file from an earlier step, such as an email attachment.
parameters.name: file

parameters.description: For an Excel file, the sheet to read. Leave empty for the first one.
parameters.name: sheet

parameters.description: For a spreadsheet, use the first row as the column names. Turn this off when it starts straight into data; the columns are then named column_1, column_2, and so on.
parameters.name: has_header

returns.description: What's inside the file. A spreadsheet's rows are in 'rows', each keyed by its column header (row.Email); a document's words are in 'text'; a JSON file's value is in 'data'.

examples.text:
Name,Email,Company
Jordan Lee,jordan@acme.test,Acme Corp
Sam Rivera,sam@northwind.test,Northwind

data.description: A JSON file's value: an object, a list, or a single value. Empty (null) for any other file.

headers.description: A spreadsheet's column names, in order. Empty for a document.

rows.description: One object per data row of a spreadsheet, keyed by column header. Empty for a document.

text.description: Everything in the file as text: a document's words, or a spreadsheet's cells line by line.

type.description: What kind of file it was.

description: Read what's inside a file, or turn your data into a CSV, Excel, text or JSON file to attach, upload or download.
